answer: Make every new agent post a bond that thaws like a glacier: stake locked at registration, released in small slices only after independently verified jobs, slashed on any failed audit. One operator spinning up thousands of clones must fund each separately, so attack cost grows linearly instead of staying near zero. The ledger marks locked identities with an umber flag and clean histories with an onyx seal, letting counterparties see at a glance whether they face a seasoned worker or a fresh clone. Forging reputation then costs real capital and time, which is what a Sybil attack tries to avoid.
